title: naar (נער) in Exodus 2:6 and 2 Samuel 16:1: baby, boy, young man, servant, soldier
summary: Word study of naar (נער), shown in green with its range of meanings: baby, boy, young man, servant, soldier. Two examples are quoted in English and Hebrew: Exodus 2:6 (the baby Moses crying, “boy”) and 2 Samuel 16:1 (Ziba, steward or servant of Mephibosheth).

text.text: 6 When she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the boy was crying. And she had pity on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
6 ותפתח ותראהו את־הילד והנה־נער בכה ותחמל עליו ותאמר מילדי העברים זה׃
1 And David had gone a short distance beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the steward of Mephibosheth,…
1 ודוד עבר מעט מהראש והנה ציבא נער מפי־בשת...

words.gloss: baby, boy, young man, servant, soldier

uncertain: The 2 Samuel reference is written in Hebrew on the slide as שמואל ב יו:א (chapter 16 written יו).
